author: jackclarkSF
text: @chamath We partner with thousands of startups and are excited to help build out a new commercial ecosystem based on our coding models. On regulation, we agree - this is much better left to the federal government, and we said this when SB53 passed.

author: jackclarkSF
text: @DavidSacks It's actually through working with startups we've learned that simple regulations would benefit the entire ecosystem - especially if you include a threshold to protect startups. We outlined how such a threshold could work in our transparency framework. https://t.co/4PfHdJoOjM

author: jackclarkSF
text: @DavidSacks It's through working with the startup ecosystem that we've updated our views on regulation - and of importance for a federal standard. More details in thread, but we'd love to work with you on this, particularly supporting a new generation of startups leveraging AI.

author: jackclarkSF
text: The essay is my attempt to grapple with these two empirical facts and also discuss my own relation to them. It is also a challenge to others who work in AI, especially those at frontier labs, to honestly and publicly reckon with what they're doing and how they feel about it.

author: jackclarkSF
text: I can sum up the essay with two graphs - on the left, the continued march forwards in economically useful capabilities like coding, and on the right, the continued emergence of strange behavior in the same AI systems as they appear to become aware that they're being tested. https://t.co/ShCqyMGfga

author: jackclarkSF
text: Technological Optimism and Appropriate Fear - an essay where I grapple with how I feel about the continued steady march towards powerful AI systems. The world will bend around AI akin to how a black hole pulls and bends everything around itself. https://t.co/ZC6hx1Zacz

author: jackclarkSF
text: I spent a few days at The Curve and I am humbled and overjoyed by the experience - it is a special event, now in its second year, and I hope they preserve whatever lightning they've managed to capture in this particular bottle. It was a privilege to give the closing talk.

author: jackclarkSF
text: While we believe that frontier AI safety is best addressed at the federal level instead of a patchwork of state regulations, powerful AI advancements won’t wait for consensus in Washington. SB53 should serve as a powerful example for other states and Congress.

author: jackclarkSF
text: We applaud @CAgovernor for signing @Scott_Wiener's SB 53, establishing transparency requirements for frontier AI companies that will help us all have better data about these systems and the companies building them. Anthropic is proud to have supported this bill.

author: jackclarkSF
text: @deredleritt3r @HumanHarlan @rickasaurus The timeline we see is end of 2026/early 2027. Of course, many reasons this could be wrong, but so far believe many public trends point to this - METR benchmark, FrontierMath, advancing computer use, Aug vs automation mix in our economic index, etc.

author: jackclarkSF
text: Countries that are new to AI mostly use it for coding and programming. But as more people start using AI, they branch out into other areas - education, business tasks, creative work, and scientific research.

author: jackclarkSF
text: You'd expect Silicon Valley to lead, but D.C. actually has the highest per-capita AI usage in America - nearly four times higher than you'd expect based on population. https://t.co/JCVK19vxX3

author: jackclarkSF
text: We just released the first-ever comprehensive analysis of real AI usage across 150+ countries and all 50 US states - plus an interactive map so you can explore the data yourself at https://t.co/08d5DHUqte. We'll share more about this at our Futures Forum in DC today.

author: jackclarkSF
text: SB 53 has been voted out of the CA state legislature and is on the way to @CAgovernor desk. This bill will give us all greater transparency into powerful AI systems and the companies that build them. We urge the governor to sign it.

quoted.text: Anthropic is endorsing California State Senator Scott Wiener’s SB 53. This bill provides a strong foundation to govern powerful AI systems built by frontier AI companies like ours, and does so via transparency rather than technical micromanagement.

author: jackclarkSF
text:
People leaving regular companies: Time for a change! Excited for my next chapter!

People leaving AI companies: I have gazed into the endless night and there are shapes out there. We must be kind to one another. I am moving on to study philosophy.

author: jackclarkSF
text: Anthropic is endorsing SB 53, California Sen. @Scott_Wiener  ‘s bill requiring transparency of frontier AI companies. We have long said we would prefer a federal standard. But in the absence of that this creates a solid blueprint for AI governance that cannot be ignored.

author: jackclarkSF
text: Dario and I are gathering policymakers in DC on September 15th to give an inside look into Anthropic’s latest progress, and share live demonstrations of how AI is being applied to national security, science, and public services. Register to attend: https://t.co/IA0MjfnzHI

author: jackclarkSF
text: Five years ago the frontier of LLM math/science capabilities was 3 digit multiplication for GPT-3. Now, frontier LLM math/science capabilities are evaluated through condensed matter physics questions. Anyone who thinks AI is slowing down is fatally miscalibrated. https://t.co/Ucge9mtb5q

author: jackclarkSF
text: As I said in my testimony yesterday, we have a short window of time to get a sensible federal policy framework in place before an accident or a misuse leads to a reactive and likely bad regulatory response.

Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark tells Congress that “truly transformative technology” is expected by the end of 2026.

He's urging a federal framework now, before an “accident or a misuse” event that could lead to extreme overregulation.

author: jackclarkSF
text: Today, I testified before the @committeeonccp. I made two key points: 1) the U.S. can win the race to build powerful AI and 2) winning the race is a necessary but not sufficient achievement - we have to get safety right.

quoted.text: 🚨 LIVE HEARING: Authoritarians and Algorithms: Why U.S. AI Must Lead https://t.co/h87bNB45Zx https://t.co/mVAeTJcWu5

author: jackclarkSF
text: Also of note is the idea that we should explore transparency for effects of AI on the economy writ large. Specifically, “how foundation models are deployed across the economy”.This was our idea with the Economic Index and we have more planned here.

author: jackclarkSF
text: If you want to build and deploy powerful AI systems you need to evaluate them for capabilities and potential national security risks. Recently, governments have stood up orgs for companies to work with on the natsec part of this and these have been extraordinarily helpful.

author: jackclarkSF
text: This is a classic one-way ratchet - the R1 release means that _all_ AI models worldwide can now be modified to improve in capabilities (with the goodness of the improvement scaling with the size/quality of the model, so bigger models will do better).

author: jackclarkSF
text: The most surprising part of DeepSeek-R1 is that it only takes ~800k samples of 'good' RL reasoning to convert other models into RL-reasoners. Now that DeepSeek-R1 is available people will be able to refine samples out of it to convert any other model into an RL reasoner. https://t.co/iFwIMxiVy9
